subject: maths
source: CISCE Curriculum for Primary Classes I-V (2016), official

covers: Read and write numbers up to six digits (lakh) using the Indian system
Know how the international system groups digits differently, and compare the two
Write numbers in expanded form and back using place value
Compare numbers and arrange them in ascending and descending order
Form the greatest and smallest six-digit numbers from given digits
Read and write Roman numerals I, V and X, up to 39
Find half, one-fourth and three-fourths in pictures, folded paper and groups of objects
Know like, unlike, unit and equivalent fractions, and add and subtract like fractions
Add and subtract numbers up to four digits, with and without regrouping
Build multiplication tables up to 10 by spotting patterns instead of rote learning
Multiply two- and three-digit numbers by the standard method and the lattice method
Divide one number by a single-digit number using dots, grouping, multiplication facts and repeated subtraction
Use all four operations in problems about money, length, mass and capacity
Write word problems for a given number statement
Estimate sums, differences and products, and check them in their head
Find factors, prime factors and multiples of numbers
Tell prime numbers from composite numbers
Test whether a number divides exactly by 2, 3, 4, 5, 9 and 10
Find the highest common factor (HCF) and lowest common multiple (LCM) by listing and by common division
Identify shapes around them and describe their features
Find the centre, radius and diameter of a circle, and how they relate
Find which shapes tile a region, and tile a region with one or more shapes
Make shapes with a 7-piece tangram
Draw a cube or cuboid from a given net
Show reflection symmetry through paper folding, paper cutting and ink blots
Draw top, front and side views of simple objects
Convert metres to centimetres and back
Solve problems on lengths and distances in daily life using the four operations
Estimate the distance between two places, then check by measuring
Weigh objects on a balance using grams and kilograms
Measure the volume of containers in litres and millilitres, and relate these units to everyday objects
Convert between days, hours and minutes
Read clock time to the minute, use a.m. and p.m., and link the 12-hour and 24-hour clocks
Find the area and perimeter of simple shapes, using a square or a book as a unit
Show collected data as a pictograph using stickers or pictures
Read bar graphs and say what is more or less
Draw a bar graph from data they have collected
Draw conclusions from graphs found in newspapers and magazines
Identify patterns that have more than one feature, such as growing or reducing patterns
Make a rule to extend a growing or reducing pattern of shapes or numbers
See that patterns in numbers and shapes lead to general rules, the start of algebra

gaps: Teaching processes and learning resources are left out; the file lists only what a child learns.
Some fraction symbols in the text extract are garbled; the file uses the written outcomes only.
